brief.headline: The test this page published in advance has resolved, and it resolved against the tightness case: on Monday's official the aluminium curve crossed out of backwardation into an outright $10.50 CONTANGO - the first of this cycle - while LME stock quietly resumed drawing, leaving the curve and the inventory line pointing in opposite directions for the first time in the window.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: the front of the curve, decisively. Monday 21-September's official put cash at $3,262.50 and three-month at $3,273.00, so cash now sits $10.50 BELOW three-month. Four sessions ago the backwardation was $21.00; it went $18.50, $18.50, $3.00 and has now crossed. Cash fell $22.50 on the day against three-month's $9.00, so the flat price and the spread moved in the SAME direction again - which rules out the tidy 'positioning artefact' explanation. Three-month is still $12.00 above the 3,261 line the page has tracked for six runs, but that is the narrowest margin of the sequence.

WHY IT IS NOT A SIMPLE 'TIGHTNESS IS OVER' STORY: LME stock DREW 400 tonnes to 242,200 on the same ring, resuming after exactly one flat session, and copper did the opposite of aluminium on the same board - its backwardation widened more than fourfold to $58.00 while its stock built. A general loosening of base metals does not look like that. The currency channel does not explain it either: the LME euro fixing rose to 1.14900 from 1.14610, so the dollar WEAKENED and aluminium fell anyway. That leaves financing cost, positioning and returning physical supply as the live candidates.

WHAT IS NEW OFF-EXCHANGE, AND IT IS A TARIFF STORY WITH A HEADCOUNT ATTACHED: on 22-September Novelis was reported to be cutting production and about 80 jobs - roughly a third of the workforce, 10 salaried and around 70 hourly temporary layoffs - at its Kingston, Ontario plant, citing the cost of US Section 232 tariffs on Canadian aluminium entering the United States. The plant stays open at reduced volumes. This is the clearest published example yet of a 50% headline rate showing up as physical capacity coming off rather than as a price line, and it lands eight days before the next dated step in the US-Canada schedule.

WHAT TO WATCH: today's 13:20 London official, which decides whether the contango was a one-session crossing or the start of a regime - a return to backwardation beyond $15.00 reverses it, a wider contango confirms it. Then the Q4-2026 Japanese premium settlement, due late September or early October against a pending $280-310/t range and a settled Q3 record of $395/t; and the Xi state visit to the United States on 23-25 September, with Chinese and US trade principals having already met in New York on 20-September. Energy moved hard and cheaper overnight - Brent about $99.95, down 3.77%, and European gas down 7.90% - which loosens the cost floor with a one-to-two-month lag rather than today.

lme.commentary: THE THREE-DAY CARRY IS OVER AND THE FIRST NEW BOARD IN FOUR DAYS ANSWERED THE QUESTION THIS PAGE ASKED IN ADVANCE. On Friday and again on Monday this page set out three possible outcomes for the cash-to-three-month spread - re-widen beyond $15.00, hold near flat, or cross into outright contango - and stated that Monday's 13:20 official would resolve it. IT CROSSED. Cash settled $3,262.50 and three-month $3,273.00, so cash is $10.50 BELOW three-month: an outright CONTANGO, the first of this cycle, after a four-session sequence of $21.00, $18.50, $18.50 and $3.00. THE MECHANICS ARE WORTH SEPARATING FROM THE HEADLINE. Cash did the work: it fell $22.50 or 0.68% while three-month fell $9.00 or 0.27%. Spread and flat price moved in the same direction for a second consecutive session, which is what makes this hard to dismiss as positioning. Three-month at $3,273.00 nevertheless held above the 3,261 level for a seventh consecutive session, by $12.00 - the narrowest margin yet, and the post-weekend test named on Monday was therefore passed, barely. Year-to-date three-month is up 8.72%, down from 9.02% on Friday. AND THEN THE PART THAT COMPLICATES THE STORY: LME warehouse stock DREW 400 TONNES to 242,200 on the same ring. The 18-September zero was the only flat print in the fifteen-session window and it arrived on the ring that collapsed the backwardation, which made a clean 'the tightness has ended' reading available. A resumed draw one session later removes that convenience. The curve and the inventory line are now pointing in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and this page will not pick whichever one flatters a narrative. The honest reading is that the curve moved on financing cost and positioning while visible metal is still being consumed. THE CROSS-CHECKS REINFORCE THAT. Copper's backwardation WIDENED from $14.00 to $58.00 on the same board while copper stock BUILT 775 tonnes; zinc's backwardation stayed wide at $87.00; and the LME euro fixing rose to 1.14900 from 1.14610, meaning the dollar weakened and aluminium fell anyway. None of the easy general explanations survive. What happened on 21-September was aluminium-specific. PROVENANCE, STATED PLAINLY: the English per-metal aluminium daily table was serving a STALE cached snapshot this morning whose newest row was still 18-September, the reverse of the 31-July incident. The usual completeness test was therefore unavailable and the board was validated five other ways instead - EN and DE overviews identical on 21-September, the 18-September comparison columns reproducing yesterday's carried figures exactly, all five stock lines reconciling arithmetically against yesterday's levels and today's reported changes, Westmetall's own zinc and lead monthly-averages pages publishing fifteen-session September means that require the 21-September print, and an independent 22-September SMM comment recording an LME close of about $3,274.5/mt. Today's official publishes at 13:20 London, about nine and a half hours after this page was built.

drivers.text: THE EXCHANGE HAS CROSSED FROM PAYING ALMOST NOTHING FOR IMMEDIACY TO PAYING TO DEFER - AND THAT IS A CATEGORY CHANGE, NOT A DEGREE CHANGE — On Monday 21-September's official the cash-to-three-month spread went from a $3.00 BACKWARDATION to a $10.50 CONTANGO: cash $3,262.50 against three-month $3,273.00. The four-session sequence is $21.00, $18.50, $3.00, minus $10.50. A backwardation is the physical market paying to have metal now; a contango is the market paying to hold it later. For a quarterly premium negotiation running into a late-September or early-October settlement, this is the strongest published argument the buy side has had in this cycle, and unlike a view it carries a date and a settlement price. WHAT WOULD REVERSE IT IS EQUALLY PUBLISHED AND SPECIFIC: a return to backwardation beyond $15.00 on a settled official.

drivers.text: THE LARGEST QUANTIFIED TRANCHE OF RETURNING GULF SUPPLY WAS RE-CONFIRMED - AND THE PACE OF WHAT FOLLOWS IT IS NOW GUIDED TO SLOW — SMM's 22-September morning summary independently records Alba's operating capacity recovering to around 1.3 million tonnes, corroborating the CEO-sourced position reported on 18-September of roughly 80% of a pre-war 1,623 kt plant on Lines 4, 5 and 6 with exports via Jeddah and Sohar. logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: REVIEWED TUESDAY 22-SEPTEMBER-2026. THE CLEAREST NEW EVIDENCE THIS RUN IS NOT A TRANSIT COUNT - IT IS A FREIGHT RATE ON A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT TRADE LANE, WHICH IS WHY IT MATTERS. SMM's 17-September bauxite weekly records that Guinea-to-China ocean freight rates rose to around $39-42/wmt in mid-September as MIDDLE EAST TENSIONS ESCALATED AGAIN and demand for shipping capacity from other cargoes increased, with mine shipping costs consolidating at highs. A Guinea-to-China voyage does not pass through Hormuz. The rate rose anyway, because regional disruption withdraws tonnage from the global pool and reprices capacity everywhere. THAT IS THE MECHANISM WORTH UNDERSTANDING: a lane constraint raises the delivered cost of material that was produced perfectly normally and never went near the affected water. The prior dated evidence stands unamended: Reuters tracking cited in analysis published 20-September put daily commodity vessel transits at 3-6 ships between 2 and 18 September against a ten-day moving average that normally runs 12-18, a third to a half of normal sustained over more than a fortnight; a tanker was reportedly struck by an unknown projectile 16 nautical miles north-east of Khasab, Oman on 18-September and caught fire; and 18-September commodity reporting cited satellite imagery indicating Saudi Arabia moved about 2.8 million barrels a day through the strait over six days against roughly 700,000 in August, with around 60 million barrels sold from Ras Tanura for September-October loading via ship-to-ship transfer OUTSIDE the strait. THE ATTRIBUTION OF THE STRIKE REMAINS UNCONFIRMED. FOR ALUMINIUM THE READ STILL CUTS BOTH WAYS: Aluminium Bahrain is exporting via Jeddah on the Red Sea and Sohar in Oman precisely to route around this chokepoint, so the largest quantified tranche of returning Gulf supply is reaching the market regardless. headlines.title: THE ALUMINIUM CURVE CROSSED INTO OUTRIGHT CONTANGO ON MONDAY'S OFFICIAL - THE FIRST OF THIS CYCLE. Cash settled $3,262.50 against three-month $3,273.00, so cash sits $10.50 BELOW three-month, against a $3.00 backwardation the session before and $21.00 four sessions ago. This page published the three-way test in advance - re-widen beyond $15.00, hold near flat, or cross - and it crossed. Cash did the work, falling $22.50 or 0.68% against three-month's $9.00 or 0.27%, so spread and flat price moved in the SAME direction for a second consecutive session, which removes the positioning-artefact explanation. The exchange has stopped paying for immediacy and is now paying to defer. The published reversal condition is a return to backwardation beyond $15.00 on a settled official.

LME WAREHOUSE STOCK RESUMED DRAWING ON THE SAME RING THAT LOOSENED THE CURVE, FALLING 400 TONNES TO 242,200. The 18-September zero was the only flat print in the fifteen-session window and it arrived on the session that collapsed the backwardation, which made a clean 'the tightness has ended' reading available. One session later that reading no longer fits: the curve and the inventory line now point in OPPOSITE directions. The level remains close to multi-decade lows and about 9,000 tonnes below the August monthly mean of 251,215. A drawdown that continues while the front loosens argues the curve moved on financing cost and positioning rather than on visible metal.

COPPER DID THE OPPOSITE OF ALUMINIUM ON THE SAME BOARD, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL CROSS-CHECK AVAILABLE. Copper's cash-to-three-month backwardation WIDENED from $14.00 to $58.00 - more than fourfold in one ring - while copper stock BUILT 775 tonnes and three-month rose 1.48%, the strongest line on the board. Zinc held a wide $87.00 backwardation. Nickel and lead remain in contango. A general loosening of base metals does not look like this, and the LME euro fixing rose to 1.14900 from 1.14610 - a WEAKER dollar, which should have supported a dollar-priced metal. Neither the sector nor the currency explains what happened to aluminium on 21-September.

NOVELIS IS REPORTED ON 22-SEPTEMBER TO BE CUTTING PRODUCTION AND ABOUT 80 JOBS AT ITS KINGSTON, ONTARIO ALUMINIUM PLANT, EXPLICITLY CITING THE COST OF US SECTION 232 TARIFFS ON CANADIAN ALUMINIUM ENTERING THE UNITED STATES. The cuts affect roughly ONE-THIRD of the plant's workforce: 10 salaried positions and temporary layoffs of around 70 hourly workers. The facility remains operational at reduced volumes, with hourly workers potentially recalled if production increases. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE PLANT: it is the clearest published instance so far of the 50% headline rate showing up as PHYSICAL CAPACITY DECISIONS rather than as a premium line, and it lands eight days before the next dated step in the US-Canada schedule on 29-September.

A DATED, HIGH-LEVEL MACRO CATALYST IS NOW ON THE CALENDAR FOR THIS WEEK. President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from 23 to 25 September at President Trump's invitation - his first visit to the US in three years and his first STATE visit in eleven - marking reciprocal visits by the two heads of state within half a year. Groundwork is already laid: on 20-September local time Chinese lead person for China-US economic and trade affairs Vice Premier He Lifeng held economic and trade consultations in New York with Treasury Secretary Bessent and Trade Representative Greer. Market commentary attributes part of aluminium's recent support to expectations of easing China-US relations. An unusually well-dated catalyst for a market whose regional prices are currently set by tariff policy.

CHINESE INGOT DESTOCKING WIDENED INTO THE HOLIDAY. As of Monday 21-September, China's social inventory of aluminium ingots fell 12,000 tonnes from the previous Thursday and 55,000 tonnes from the previous Monday. The named drivers are a disruption to aluminium ingot shipments out of Xinjiang and downstream stockpiling ahead of the National Day holiday, and the destocking trend is expected to continue in the short term. TREAT THE DRIVERS AS PART OF THE DATUM: both a rail bottleneck and pre-holiday restocking reverse by design, so this is a draw whose durability is tested after the holiday rather than confirmed by it.

THE PACE OF EX-CHINA OPERATING-CAPACITY INCREASES IS NOW GUIDED TO SLOW, AND THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS. SMM's 22-September summary records that Middle East production resumptions continued to accelerate, but that SOME NEW PROJECTS WERE DELAYED and the pace of operating-capacity increases is expected to slow in the coming months. The same note independently corroborates Alba's operating capacity recovering to around 1.3 million tonnes. Less returning supply than the restart list implies, arriving later than the list implies - supportive of price, but it also means the largest quantified tranche of returning Gulf supply is already in the market rather than still ahead of it.

CHINESE PHYSICAL PREMIUMS SPLIT SHARPLY BY REGION AND THE WEAK END IS GENUINELY WEAK. Central China transactions on Monday settled around a DISCOUNT of 70-100 yuan/mt against the SHFE aluminium October contract, with downstream processing enterprises showing insufficient restocking willingness having already bought substantially at earlier low prices, and suppliers preferring to reduce inventory ahead of the holiday rather than hold prices firm. South China was the mirror image, holding premiums of 210-250 yuan/mt against the 2610 contract on scarce domestic supply. SHFE aluminium closed 24,195 yuan/mt overnight, down 0.45%, and SMM A00 fell 60 yuan to 24,320 yuan/mt. SMM A00 spot premiums transacted between parity and a 20 yuan/mt premium.

THE ENERGY COMPLEX FELL HARD AND BROADLY, WHICH LOOSENS THE COST FLOOR WITH A LAG RATHER THAN TODAY. Brent is quoted at about $99.95/bbl, DOWN 3.77% and back below the $100 line, with WTI down 4.80% to about $95.48; European gas TTF fell 7.90% to about EUR 73.23 and natural gas fell 2.19%. FOR THE SMELTER COST STACK THE READ IS DIRECTIONAL BUT SLOW: crude sets the tone for calcined petroleum coke and coal tar pitch, together roughly a fifth of cash cost, with a one-to-two-month lag - so this shows up in carbon settlements in October and November, not in September. THE GAS MOVE IS THE MORE IMMEDIATE ONE and it runs the other way to last week: cheaper European gas relieves pressure on Alunorte's temporary gas-supplier arrangement and on Qatalum's reduced-gas curtailment.

EU CARBON-BORDER EXPOSURE IS NOT FALLING AS FAST AS EU FOIL IMPORT VOLUMES, AND THE MIX IS WHY. Eurostat Comext data updated 15-September put extra-EU aluminium foil imports (HS7607) at 137.28 kt in January-July 2026, DOWN 22.2% year on year; theoretical net certificate exposure for identified non-exempt origins fell 24.1% to 326.74 kt CO2e. BUT trade-weighted UNIT exposure ROSE 0.7%, from 2.6377 to 2.6550 t CO2e per tonne, because the origin mix shifted: China and Turkiye together now account for 75.8% of calculable exposure, up from 69.7% a year earlier. Under default values China's net unit exposure of 4.5559 t CO2e/t is about 2.5 times Turkiye's 1.8191. Published certificate prices are EUR 75.36 for Q1-2026 and EUR 75.28 for Q2; the Q3 price had not been published as of 18-September. Falling import volumes do not by themselves establish that unit carbon-cost exposure has eased.

GUINEA-TO-CHINA OCEAN FREIGHT IS STILL CLIMBING ON MIDDLE EAST TENSIONS, RAISING LANDED ORE COST WITHOUT ANY CHANGE IN THE ORE ITSELF. SMM's 17-September bauxite weekly records Guinea-China rates rising to around $39-42/wmt in mid-September as tensions escalated again and demand for shipping capacity from other cargoes increased. The SMM imported bauxite index printed $72.35/mt, up $0.28 on the week; Guinean FOB quotes were $35-45/mt and CIF $70-73/mt, both flat week on week; Guinea's September long-term contract offers continued to settle at $72-74/mt. Weekly Guinean port departures rebounded 1.8784 Mt to 5.5696 Mt and Chinese arrivals rose 1.5265 Mt to 4.9614 Mt. Chinese alumina refinery ore inventory sits around 94 days, which caps how hard the ore side can push.

CHINESE SCRAP CIRCULATION IS TIGHTENING FOR A REGULATORY REASON RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, WHICH SUPPORTS THE SECONDARY COMPLEX AND, INDIRECTLY, PRIMARY DEMAND. Tax-invoice inspections in the central China region continued to intensify, raising compliance procurement requirements and making invoiced scrap supply relatively tight; SMM expects a sharp decline in regional scrap supply to disrupt circulation materially. On 21-September the A00-to-mixed-extrusion-scrap spread in Foshan was about 2,572 yuan/mt and the A00-to-shredded-tense spread about 1,351 yuan/mt. ADC12 held at 24,500 yuan/mt. Working against it, the cast aluminium alloy 'September peak season' fell short of expectations with no concentrated restocking. Watch whether scrap yards slow shipments.

Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL - THE CONFIRMATION OR THE REVERSAL OF THE CONTANGO, AND THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE SCHEDULED EVENT ON THIS PAGE. Monday's settlement crossed the curve from a $3.00 backwardation to a $10.50 contango, the first of this cycle. THE QUESTION IS NOW NARROWER THAN IT WAS YESTERDAY AND IT IS STATED IN ADVANCE AGAIN: does the contango WIDEN, confirming a regime change at the front of the curve; does it HOLD near current levels; or does the spread RETURN TO BACKWARDATION BEYOND $15.00, which is this page's published reversal condition and would restore the bull case toward 30%? Watch the stock line with equal attention: a second consecutive draw would deepen the disagreement between the curve and the inventory, which is the central unresolved tension on this page.

THE 3,261 LEVEL IS AT ITS NARROWEST MARGIN OF THE SEQUENCE. Three-month settled $3,273.00 on Monday, just $12.00 above it, having settled above it on every session since 15-September. A daily settlement BELOW 3,261 is this page's published condition for raising the bear scenario beyond 30%, and on the weekly Elliott count it is the level the position-degree structure turns on. The stated SMM range for LME aluminium this week is $3,250-3,320/t - a band whose floor sits below the level, which is itself informative about how close this is.

PRESIDENT XI'S STATE VISIT TO THE UNITED STATES - HIS FIRST STATE VISIT IN ELEVEN YEARS AND THE BEST-DATED MACRO CATALYST ON THIS PAGE. Groundwork was laid on 20-September when Vice Premier He Lifeng, China's lead person for China-US economic and trade affairs, held consultations in New York with Treasury Secretary Bessent and Trade Representative Greer. FOR THIS MARKET THE RELEVANCE IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN GENERAL: regional delivered prices are currently set by tariff policy rather than by physical scarcity, so any movement on the trade file transmits directly into the premium complex. Market commentary already attributes part of aluminium's recent support to expectations of easing relations, which means disappointment is a live risk in the same window.

THE MONTHLY CARBON-INPUT SETTLEMENT CYCLE IS OPEN, OVERDUE AND HAS STILL NOT PRINTED - A FIFTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. Prebaked anode, coal tar pitch and green petcoke marks normally settle around the 17th-18th of each month. Nothing has published, so roughly a fifth of the smelter cash-cost stack is carried on marks about a month old. THE DIRECTION WHEN IT PRINTS IS NOW STRONGLY SIGNPOSTED: Brent has fallen four consecutive sessions to about $99.95/bbl and is back below $100. Signposted is not settled, and this page will append a mark to the input histories only when a dated public figure exists. Note the second-order point: a falling cost floor lowers marginal-cost support under the price.

THE NEXT DATED STEP IN THE US-CANADA TARIFF SCHEDULE: a US vehicle and dairy import ban takes effect, following Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn in force since 08-September and the 08-September White House annex that lifted previously exempt downstream aluminium lines to a combined levy of up to 100%. THE CONTEXT CHANGED THIS RUN AND IT MAKES THIS DATE MORE INTERESTING, NOT LESS: on 22-September Novelis was reported to be cutting production and about 80 jobs at Kingston, Ontario explicitly on Section 232 costs. The first clearly attributed capacity consequence has arrived eight days before the next escalation.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLEMENT - STILL THE LARGEST SINGLE DATED EVENT LEFT ON THIS PAGE AND NOW INSIDE TWO WEEKS. The pending range carried here is $280-310/t against a settled Q3 record of $395/t, a fall of 22-29% if it lands inside. The range is unchanged for a seventh consecutive run because no newer dated evidence has printed. THE NEGOTIATING BACKDROP GAINED ITS STRONGEST BUYER-SIDE ARGUMENT OF THE CYCLE THIS RUN and it is a category change rather than a degree change: the exchange curve has CROSSED INTO OUTRIGHT CONTANGO. Alongside it sit producer offers of $310-325/t, Alba re-confirmed at about 1.3 Mt, softer European premiums, and a Chinese central-China spot market transacting at a 70-100 yuan/mt discount to the October contract.

CHINA'S NATIONAL DAY HOLIDAY AND THE POST-HOLIDAY REBUILD TEST - THE CLEANEST FORWARD EXPERIMENT AVAILABLE ON CHINESE DEMAND, AND THIS RUN SHARPENED IT. SMM attributes the current destocking - 12,000 tonnes on the week and 55,000 tonnes on the prior Monday - to a Xinjiang outbound shipment disruption and pre-holiday stockpiling, BOTH OF WHICH REVERSE BY DESIGN. The test is explicit: STRONG post-holiday operating rates that absorb the returning metal would mean the tightness was genuine; a MUTED return with inventory rebuilding would confirm it was seasonal and logistics-driven. The central-China spot discount of 70-100 yuan/mt and a liquid-aluminium share that fell a further 0.02 percentage points are the leading indicators pointing to the muted outcome. Note the one-to-two-week reporting lag on operating-rate surveys.

THE NEXT FEDERAL OPEN MARKET COMMITTEE MEETING, AND IT NOW BEARS DIRECTLY ON THE CENTRAL QUESTION ON THIS PAGE. With the dot plot revised to a 4.1% median for 2026 against 3.8% in June, and two meetings left in October and December, the projections imply at least one further increase before year-end. The curve has already moved the way that financing cost implies - from a $21.00 backwardation to a $10.50 contango in five sessions - so a further increase would argue against the contango reversing, and a HOLD in October would remove the cleanest structural argument against a return to backwardation. Carry acts on the curve rather than on the flat price, and the curve is exactly where this page's central question sits.

THE Q3-2026 PEER REPORTING SEASON OPENS AND ENDS THE CURRENT LULL. No peer result has been reported in the last 48 hours and the most recent on this page remains Constellium's Q2 of 29-July. Q3 will be the first reporting period that spans the full post-restart Gulf picture, the 50% Section 232 regime in steady state, and a quarter in which the exchange price averaged materially above the first half - so it is the first genuine read on whether the margin expansion reported through H1 has persisted or has started to compress from the revenue side.

risks.text: THE FRONT OF THE CURVE HAS CROSSED INTO OUTRIGHT CONTANGO AND THE TREND IS RAISED TO UP - THIS IS NOW THE PRIMARY RISK ON THE PAGE. The five-run sequence is $21.00, $18.50, $18.50, $3.00 and minus $10.50: from the market paying a clear premium for immediate metal to the market paying to defer it. THIS PAGE NAMED THE PATTERN FOUR RUNS AGO WHEN IT WAS STILL ARGUABLY NOISE, PUBLISHED THE THREE-WAY TEST IN ADVANCE, AND THE TEST RESOLVED AGAINST THE TIGHTNESS CASE. Two features make the 21-September print hard to dismiss: spread and flat price moved in the SAME direction for a second consecutive session, removing the positioning-artefact explanation; and the LME euro fixing STRENGTHENED to 1.14900 from 1.14610, so a weaker dollar failed to support the price and the currency channel is eliminated rather than blamed. WHY THE TREND IS UP AND NOT MERELY FLAT: a crossing is a category change, not a degree change, and it happened on a settled official rather than an indication. WHAT TURNS IT DOWN IS PUBLISHED AND SPECIFIC: a return to backwardation beyond $15.00 on a settled official. TODAY'S 13:20 LONDON OFFICIAL IS THE CONFIRMATION OR THE REVERSAL.

THE FEDERAL RESERVE'S REVISED PATH IS NOW VISIBLY CONSISTENT WITH THE CURVE, AND THE TREND IS HELD AT UP. The Committee raised the target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16-September, unanimously at 12-0, and lifted its median 2026 federal funds projection from 3.8% in June to 4.1%, with 3.9% for 2027 and 3.6% for 2028; two meetings remain on the 2026 calendar. THE CHANNEL THAT BITES HERE IS CARRY, NOT THE DOLLAR - and this run supplies the evidence for that distinction rather than merely asserting it. The dollar WEAKENED on the LME fixing and aluminium fell anyway, so the currency channel did nothing. Meanwhile this page carries a nominal ten-year at about 4.967%, essentially unchanged, with real ten-year yields reported at 4.3-4.4%. A financing cost at that level is structurally hostile to a backwardation, because nobody is paid enough to hold the stock a backwardation exists to attract. THE CURVE HAS NOW MOVED THE WAY THAT FINANCING COST IMPLIES. That consistency is the most useful cross-check on this page today - and it is an inference from consistency, not a demonstrated causal link, which is why the trend is up rather than the risk being called resolved.

TARIFF POLICY IS NO LONGER ONLY SETTING REGIONAL PRICE - IT HAS STARTED REMOVING PHYSICAL CAPACITY, AND THE TREND IS RAISED TO UP ON A DATED, ATTRIBUTED EXAMPLE. The Section 232 headline rate is re-verified and UNCHANGED at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU; the 08-September annex lifting previously exempt downstream lines toward a combined 100% and Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn remain in force. NO NEW INSTRUMENT PRINTED. WHAT IS NEW IS THE CONSEQUENCE: on 22-September Novelis was reported to be cutting production and about 80 jobs at Kingston, Ontario - roughly a third of that workforce - EXPLICITLY CITING THE COST OF THOSE TARIFFS on Canadian metal entering the United States. That is the first clearly attributed capacity reduction of this cycle, and it sits awkwardly against public forecasting that has the US Midwest premium averaging its highest-ever level in 2026 on the same rate: the policy is simultaneously lifting the US delivered price and removing North American conversion capacity. At $3,262.50 cash the 50% leg alone is about $1,631.25/t. Next dated step: a US vehicle and dairy import ban on 29-September.

THE STOCK DRAWDOWN HAS RESUMED, WHICH IS THE ONE CLEAR PIECE OF GOOD NEWS FOR THE TIGHTNESS CASE - AND THE TREND IS CUT TO DOWN. Visible LME stock fell 400 tonnes to 242,200 on the 21-September session after exactly ONE flat print. The 18-September zero was the only flat session in the fifteen-session window and it arrived on the ring that collapsed the backwardation, which made a clean 'the tightness has ended' reading available; one session later that reading no longer fits. The level remains close to multi-decade lows and about 9,000 tonnes below the August monthly mean of 251,215. THE TENSION WITH THE CURVE IS REAL AND IS NOT RESOLVED HERE: visible metal is still being consumed while the front has stopped paying for immediacy. The honest reading is that the curve moved on financing cost and positioning rather than on inventory. The chart floor is held at 235,000 with 7,200 tonnes of headroom and is re-checked every run.

THE GULF SUPPLY PICTURE REMAINS CONTESTED IN PUBLIC, BUT THE TREND IS CUT FROM FLAT TO DOWN BECAUSE THE FORWARD PACE IS NOW GUIDED TO SLOW. On the unwinding side the dated position strengthened: SMM's 22-September summary independently corroborates Aluminium Bahrain at about 1.3 million tonnes of recovered operating capacity, matching the CEO-sourced 18-September report of roughly 80% of a pre-war 1,623 kt plant with exports via Jeddah and Sohar; Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah remains a partial restart at a publicly stated 18% of capacity with a return guided for early 2027. AGAINST IT, CRU GROUP IS REPORTED AS HOLDING THAT GULF PRODUCTION IS DOWN AROUND 25% YEAR ON YEAR. Both cannot be fully right and this page will not quietly pick the one that fits its narrative. WHAT IS NEW AND WHY THE ARROW TURNS DOWN: SMM states that while resumptions continued to ACCELERATE, SOME NEW PROJECTS WERE DELAYED and the pace of operating-capacity increases outside China is expected to SLOW in the coming months. The biggest single tranche is already in the market; less follows behind it than the restart list implies. The published deficit spread of 300,000-500,000 tonnes base against up to 1.4 million tonnes bull remains the honest encoding of the disagreement.

THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM OVERHANG IS MARKED BACK TO UP THIS RUN, AND THE EVIDENCE IS A PRICE RATHER THAN AN INVENTORY. Central China transactions on 21-September settled around a DISCOUNT of 70-100 yuan/mt against the SHFE October contract, with SMM recording that downstream processing enterprises showed insufficient restocking willingness having already bought substantially at earlier low prices, and that suppliers preferred to reduce inventory ahead of the holiday rather than hold prices firm. A physical market transacting at a discount to the futures because buyers will not step up is a demand statement, not a logistics one. THE CONFIRMING NUMBER IS THE ONE THIS PAGE HAS TRACKED THROUGHOUT: the liquid-aluminium share FELL a further 0.02 percentage points on select downstream curtailments. If consumption were accelerating, liquid usage would rise. THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT: national ingot social inventory fell 12,000 tonnes on the week and 55,000 tonnes on the prior Monday, and South China held premiums of 210-250 yuan/mt on scarce domestic supply - but the named drivers of the draw are a Xinjiang rail disruption and pre-holiday restocking, both of which reverse by design. The post-holiday operating rates are the test.

THE COST FLOOR IS NOW CLEARLY FALLING ON THE ENERGY LINES, AND THE TREND IS CUT TO DOWN - BUT THE CARBON DATA GAP IS THE LARGER HALF OF THIS RISK AND IT IS GETTING OLDER. Brent fell 3.77% to about $99.95 and back below $100, a fourth consecutive decline; WTI fell 4.80%; and European gas TTF fell 7.90% to about EUR 73.23, REVERSING the rise this page flagged yesterday as the only clearly climbing energy line. That gas move relieves pressure on the two named gas exposures on this page - Alunorte's TEMPORARY gas-supplier terminal-access agreement and Qatalum's curtailment at roughly 60% of 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas - and it transmits fastest of anything in the cost panel, through European smelter power. THE CARBON COMPLEX IS THE REAL GAP AND IT IS NOW FIVE RUNS OLD: prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petcoke normally settle around the 17th-18th of the month and NO NEW PUBLIC SETTLEMENT HAS PRINTED, so roughly a fifth of cash cost is carried on marks about a month old. Four consecutive sessions of falling crude signposts the direction, but signposted is not settled and no history has been appended on an interpolated basis. A FALLING COST FLOOR IS NOT UNAMBIGUOUSLY GOOD NEWS: it lowers the marginal-cost support under the price.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM SETTLEMENT IS NOW THE LARGEST UNPRICED SINGLE EVENT ON THIS PAGE AND THE TREND IS RAISED TO UP BECAUSE THE BUYER'S CASE STRENGTHENED MATERIALLY THIS RUN. The premium panel is carried for a fourth consecutive run - no price-reporting agency publishes into a 03:50 London window - and the oldest material carry is the CIF Japan spot indication at $370/t against dated September spot reporting of roughly $320-380/t and producer offers of $310-325/t for October-December shipments. The settled Q3 benchmark of $395/t is not stale, because a quarterly benchmark is fixed until the quarter turns, but it is increasingly disconnected. THE PENDING RANGE ON THIS PAGE IS $280-310/t, a fall of 22-29%, and it is unchanged for a seventh consecutive run because no newer dated evidence has printed. WHAT CHANGED IS THE NEGOTIATING BACKDROP: the exchange curve has CROSSED INTO CONTANGO, which is the strongest buyer-side argument of this cycle and carries a settlement price rather than a view. A reader looking only at the panel would see no warning in the numbers; the warning is written here.

STRAIT OF HORMUZ AND REGIONAL SHIPPING DISRUPTION IS HELD AT UP, AND THE NEW EVIDENCE THIS RUN IS THE MOST TELLING YET BECAUSE IT COMES FROM A LANE THAT DOES NOT TOUCH THE STRAIT. SMM's 17-September bauxite weekly records Guinea-to-China ocean freight rising to around $39-42/wmt in mid-September as MIDDLE EAST TENSIONS ESCALATED AGAIN and competing cargo demand absorbed capacity, with mine shipping costs consolidating at highs. A Guinea-China voyage does not pass through Hormuz; the rate rose anyway, because regional disruption withdraws tonnage from the global pool and reprices capacity everywhere. THAT IS THE MECHANISM WORTH UNDERSTANDING: a lane constraint raises the delivered cost of material produced perfectly normally and never near the affected water. The prior evidence stands: Reuters tracking cited 20-September put daily commodity transits at 3-6 ships between 2 and 18 September against a normal ten-day average of 12-18; a tanker was reportedly struck near Khasab, Oman on 18-September. THE ATTRIBUTION OF THE STRIKE REMAINS UNCONFIRMED and the transit counts are the harder half of the claim.

THE EX-CHINA RESTART PIPELINE IS VISIBLE AND DATED BUT THE TREND IS HELD AT FLAT, AND THE REASON IS THAT IT GOT SLOWER AND LARGER AT THE SAME TIME. The publicly reported list carries Aluminium Bahrain at about 1.3 Mt annualised against a 1,623 kt plant, now corroborated by a second source; Century's Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015 on a $50m investment restarting more than 50,000 t; Slovalco restarting the first 75,000 t of 175,000 t guided for Q4-2026, with its power input having moved favourably again as European gas fell 7.90%; Magnitude 7 Metals with a first potline guided before end-2026 for about 75,000 t, publicly attributed to the 50% US tariff; and EGA's DX+ Ultra licence to NALCO for a proposed 500,000 t/y Angul expansion. AGAINST THAT, SMM NOW GUIDES THAT SOME NEW PROJECTS WERE DELAYED AND THE PACE OF OPERATING-CAPACITY INCREASES WILL SLOW IN COMING MONTHS - and separately, US Section 232 has begun REMOVING North American conversion capacity, with Novelis cutting production at Kingston, Ontario. Restarts are slow, none of this lands this quarter, and the two new pieces of evidence point in opposite directions. Flat is the honest arrow.

EU CARBON-BORDER COST IS A SLOW, STRUCTURAL RISK TO EUROPEAN DELIVERED PRICE AND IT IS ADDED TO THE REGISTER THIS RUN AT FLAT. SMM analysis published 22-September, using Eurostat Comext data updated 15-September, shows extra-EU aluminium foil imports (HS7607) at 137.28 kt in January-July 2026, DOWN 22.2% year on year, with theoretical net certificate exposure for identified non-exempt origins down 24.1% to 326.74 kt CO2e. YET TRADE-WEIGHTED UNIT EXPOSURE ROSE 0.7%, from 2.6377 to 2.6550 t CO2e per tonne, because the origin mix shifted: China and Turkiye together now account for 75.8% of calculable exposure against 69.7% a year earlier, and China's default net unit exposure of 4.5559 t CO2e/t is about 2.5 times Turkiye's 1.8191. WHY IT IS FLAT RATHER THAN UP: the mechanism is known, the parameters are published, and nothing accelerated this run - aluminium carries a 10% mark-up in 2026 against a 97.5% CBAM factor, and certificate prices are EUR 75.36 for Q1 and EUR 75.28 for Q2 with Q3 unpublished as of 18-September. THE USEFUL WARNING IS METHODOLOGICAL: falling import volumes do not establish that unit carbon-cost exposure has eased, and a 'low-carbon' label is not a substitute for installation-level verified data.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

A CACHE DISCREPANCY WAS FOUND AND IT RAN IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO THE 31-JULY-2026 INCIDENT. The ENGLISH per-metal aluminium daily table was still serving a stale snapshot whose newest row was 18-September, while BOTH overview pages had already rolled to 21-September. The page's usual completeness test was therefore UNAVAILABLE this run and was not pretended otherwise.

THE BOARD WAS VALIDATED FIVE OTHER WAYS INSTEAD, AND ALL FIVE PASSED. (1) The English and German overviews, both re-requested cache-busted, agree line for line on 21-September across all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings. (2) The 18-September comparison columns on both overviews reproduce EXACTLY the figures this page carried yesterday, including the 1.14610 / 1.14600 / 1.14603 FX triplet. (3) All five stock lines reconcile arithmetically against yesterday's carried levels and today's reported changes - aluminium 242,600 less 400, copper 255,100 plus 775, zinc 115,300 plus 1,550, lead 373,625 less 900, nickel 278,826 less 300. (4) Westmetall's zinc and lead monthly-averages pages publish fifteen-session September means of $4,036.63 and $1,863.23 that arithmetically require the 21-September print. (5) A 22-September SMM comment independently records an LME aluminium close near $3,274.5/mt.

THE WHOLE BOARD SITS ON ONE UNIFORM SESSION. No intraday, unofficial, reference or contract-for-difference mark has been used anywhere in the LME board, the metals detail panel, the fifteen-session series or the copper input history. Reference and CFD quotes appear ONLY in the macro and energy panel and are labelled as such there.

THE PREMIUM PANEL IS CARRIED IN FULL AND THE CARRY IS NOW FOUR RUNS OLD ON MOST ROWS. Premium assessments are periodic, not continuous, and no price-reporting agency published into a compile window closing at 03:50 London. Every row shows its last dated public mark with the as-of date stated. The oldest material carry is the CIF Japan spot indication at $370/t against dated September spot reporting of roughly $320-380/t and producer Q4 offers of $310-325/t - a gap that the Q4 settlement, due within about two weeks, could close in a single print.

THE ALUMINA, BAUXITE AND RAW-MATERIALS PANEL IS ALSO CARRIED. The freshest hard FOB East Australia trade is 11-September at $353.50/mt, eleven days old; the freshest SMM alumina detail is the 15-September session; the freshest bauxite mark is the 17-September weekly. None of it has been interpolated or advanced.

ROUGHLY A FIFTH OF THE SMELTER CASH-COST STACK IS CARRIED ON MARKS ABOUT A MONTH OLD, FOR A FIFTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. Prebaked anode, coal tar pitch and green petcoke settlements normally print around the 17th-18th of the month and the September cycle is overdue with nothing published. Brent falling four consecutive sessions to about $99.95 signposts the eventual direction but does not settle it, and no input history has been appended on an interpolated basis.

THE CONTANGO IS ONE SESSION OLD AND THIS PAGE IS NOT YET CALLING IT A REGIME. A single settled official crossing from a $3.00 backwardation to a $10.50 contango is a genuine, pre-registered, resolved test - but it is one print. Today's 13:20 London official is the confirmation or the reversal, and the published reversal condition is a return to backwardation beyond $15.00.

THE CURVE AND THE STOCK LINE DISAGREE AND THIS PAGE HAS NOT RESOLVED THE DISAGREEMENT IN EITHER DIRECTION. The front loosened into contango on the same ring that LME stock resumed drawing, and on a board where copper's backwardation widened fourfold while copper stock built. The financing-cost explanation is the most coherent one available and is consistent with a nominal ten-year near 4.967% - but consistency is not causation, and it is presented as an inference, not a finding.
